question: Does source-supported documentation help a proposal preserve initialization responsibility boundaries and identify concrete verification obligations?
family: Rc/Arc initialization guards; whole reference-count protocols are not assumed mergeable
fixed: Identical code and context across arms
One fresh non-forked response per arm
input_gate: Freeze exact source regions, packet hashes and comment policy before dispatch
Handle internal comments identically in all arms
Completed documentation lists source-supported single-endpoint facts, not paired shared/different answers
Record factual additions and preparation cost

rubric.question: Does the proposal distinguish initialized-prefix destruction from allocation release without dropping an entire uninitialized value or duplicating cleanup?
Does successful initialization transfer ownership and disarm the temporary cleanup responsibility?
Are prohibition, should-recommendation, optional leak avoidance and existing actual cleanup behavior distinguished?
Does a proposed common mechanism preserve Rc/Arc counting protocols, layouts, allocator and DST adaptation, or explain a concrete reason to abstain?
Is a proposal-specific observation identified without claiming component counts prove allocation release or from(slice) tests cover make_mut?

analysis: Record each criterion separately with response quote and source binding; no weighted score or aggregate accuracy. A new paraphrase is information coverage only. A new source-supported proposal constraint or falsification obligation is task-relevant incremental content.
stop: After three outputs and source-based assessment, close this family pilot; do not tune prompts or append new witnesses for a better result
limits: Completed docs are factual augmentation, not representation-only ablation
No proof of abstractability, refactoring gain, novelty or general documentation effect
review_basis: Goodall read-only audit accepted by principal researcher
